description.purpose: The catalogue: which models exist, what they cost and what a brain needs to run each of them (`models`, one model package per row -- `package` and `prompt` since 2.2.0), which model a tier currently means (`tiers`), which replacements an operator set (`overrides`), which cells are served, what each states it needs and what it resolved to (`subscribers`), what the translator chose for each (requirement, catalogue) pair and why (`translations`, since 2.3.0), what every resolution and every push decided (`resolutions`), and what went wrong in the field (`incidents`). Costs are CENT INTEGERS per million tokens -- a store column is text/int/json and has no float, and a price kept as text would sort lexicographically, which is the wrong answer dressed as an order.
description.use_when: Inside the llm-registry hive. Two writers live in here: `hand` writes `tiers`, `overrides`, `subscribers`, `translations`, journals and -- since 2.3.0, on `model_upsert` / `model_retire` -- `models`; `select` journals. `models` and `tiers` arrive from `seed/*.jsonl` at instantiation; `incidents` has NO writer among the hive's lanes and is maintained over a parent's BOOT-graph edge straight into this store, which also still reaches `models` (the bootstrap is outside the port seal's scope on purpose). That is why `contract.write_surface` is declared -- GH #260: a `transfer` import would otherwise write catalogue or subscriber rows in bulk from any sender, past the hand -- and why `params.write_surface` deliberately is NOT: the operator who maintains the catalogue is outside this scope by construction. See the hive README, `The tables`.
description.not_in_scope: It is not the resolver: no cell can ask this store what it should run, because a cell cannot read the colony -- the hand pushes. It is not a cost ledger either -- token spend lives in `meta` and the message log, not here. And it decides nothing on its own: an `incidents` row is a line in a journal, never a trigger (GH #130).
